stories.title: Crypto Biz: Wall Street and Crypto Compete for the Same Market
stories.summary: Cointelegraph's Crypto Biz column looks at how Wall Street firms and crypto-native companies now chase the same customers and products. It frames traditional finance's push into digital assets as direct competition, not just adoption. The source gives no further specifics on which products or firms it names.
stories.whyItMatters: Growing overlap between Wall Street and crypto firms signals how mainstream digital assets have become.
whatToWatch: Future Crypto Biz coverage on which segments TradFi targets next
questions: Which specific products or market segments does the column say are contested?

stories.title: Bitcoin ETF Flows Turn Positive for 2026 After Erasing $5.8B Deficit
stories.summary: Spot bitcoin ETFs have wiped out a $5.8 billion year-to-date outflow deficit, pushing 2026 net flows positive, CoinDesk reports. Cointelegraph adds that the daily pace has slowed to $191 million, capping a six-day inflow streak worth $2.8 billion.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are a key read on institutional demand and can move bitcoin's price directly.
whatToWatch: Whether daily inflows reaccelerate or stall near breakeven
Next weekly flow report for signs the streak holds
questions: What is driving the rebound — new allocators or short covering?

stories.title: Bitcoin Holders Are Selling, But Not Like They Did at Past Market Tops
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports long-term bitcoin holders are taking profits, but the pattern looks different from the heavy distribution seen at prior cycle tops. CryptoSlate separately notes bitcoin faces a fresh inflation test after diesel prices hit a nominal record of $6.53.
stories.whyItMatters: Holder behavior and inflation data both shape whether bitcoin's macro backdrop stays supportive.
whatToWatch: On-chain data for signs of accelerating long-term-holder selling
Upcoming inflation prints and any Fed reaction
questions: Does the milder selling reflect confidence, or simply fewer sellers left?

stories.title: US Crypto ETFs Pull In Over $3 Billion This Week, Nearly $800M Beyond Bitcoin
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports US crypto ETFs took in more than $3 billion in weekly inflows, with almost $800 million going into non-bitcoin products.
stories.whyItMatters: Inflows spreading beyond bitcoin ETFs point to institutional demand for a wider set of digital assets.
whatToWatch: Whether non-bitcoin ETF inflows keep pace next week
A breakdown of which assets outside bitcoin drew the most money
questions: Which specific funds or assets absorbed the non-bitcoin inflows?

stories.title: Bitcoin Rally Slows as $15.6B Options Expiry Hits; XRP and Solana Keep Climbing
stories.summary: Decrypt reports bitcoin's rally has lost steam as a $15.6 billion options expiry lands, a common source of short-term volatility. XRP and Solana are still gaining even as bitcoin cools.
stories.whyItMatters: Large options expiries can whipsaw prices, and diverging altcoin strength is worth watching for signs of rotation.
whatToWatch: Bitcoin price action in the hours after expiry settles
Whether XRP and Solana gains hold or fade with bitcoin

stories.title: Is Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth a Bitcoiner? Bitcoin Magazine Digs Into His Accounts
stories.summary: Bitcoin Magazine examines Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's public accounts for signs of bitcoin advocacy, following disclosure that he holds bitcoin. The piece is speculative about his personal views and does not confirm any advocacy.
stories.whyItMatters: Senior US officials' crypto holdings and views draw scrutiny given their potential influence over crypto policy.
whatToWatch: Any public statement from Hegseth on bitcoin policy
questions: Does personal bitcoin ownership indicate any policy stance?

stories.title: Circle and Tether Freeze Hacker Wallet Linked to Bitget Heist
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports Circle and Tether moved to freeze a wallet tied to the hacker behind a large breach at crypto exchange Bitget.
stories.whyItMatters: Stablecoin issuers freezing hacker-linked wallets shows a growing tool for containing exchange breaches, though it does not fully recover losses.
whatToWatch: Whether more stolen funds get frozen or recovered
Bitget's response and any compensation plan for affected users
questions: How much of the total stolen amount does the frozen wallet represent?

stories.title: Strategy Proposes Daily Dividend, Shifting Bitcoin Funding Decisions to Investors
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, has proposed a daily dividend structure. The move would give investors more direct say over how the company's bitcoin purchases get funded.
stories.whyItMatters: Strategy is the largest corporate bitcoin holder, so changes to its funding and payout structure affect its buying capacity and investor risk.
whatToWatch: Shareholder vote or board decision on the proposal
Any change in Strategy's pace of bitcoin purchases
questions: How would a daily dividend affect Strategy's ability to keep buying bitcoin?

stories.title: KelpDAO Sues LayerZero Over 2026's Largest Exploit, a $292M rsETH Bridge Hack
stories.summary: KelpDAO has sued LayerZero and its CEO following a $292 million exploit of the rsETH bridge, according to CoinDesk and Cointelegraph. It's described as the largest crypto exploit of 2026 so far.
stories.whyItMatters: Cross-chain bridges remain a top attack surface, and this lawsuit could set precedent for liability between protocols after a DeFi exploit.
whatToWatch: Court proceedings and LayerZero's response
Whether other affected parties join the suit
questions: How exactly was the bridge exploited, and can any funds be recovered?

stories.title: Bitget Revises Security Breach Total to $388M in Affected Assets
stories.summary: Cointelegraph reports Bitget has clarified that $388 million in assets were affected by its security breach, up from the $352 million figure reported a day earlier when the exchange suspended withdrawals.
stories.whyItMatters: A breach this size tests custodial security and user trust across exchanges, and the shifting total shows how uncertain early damage estimates can be.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitget resumes withdrawals
The final confirmed loss figure and any user compensation plan
questions: Is the $388M figure final, or could it change again?

sources.title: Bitget clarifies $388M in assets affected by security breach
Bitget confirms $352M security breach, suspends withdrawals

stories.title: Magic Eden Warns Old Ethereum NFT Listings Are Exposed to a Payment Processor Exploit
stories.summary: Decrypt reports Magic Eden has warned that older Ethereum NFT listings are vulnerable to an exploit involving a payment processor, and is urging affected users to take action.
stories.whyItMatters: NFT marketplace vulnerabilities can expose holders to fund loss even on old listings, a reminder that legacy integrations carry ongoing risk.
whatToWatch: Magic Eden's fix or mitigation steps
Whether any funds are reported stolen through this exploit
questions: What specific action should affected NFT holders take?
